source_evidence.title: KG-GPT: A General Framework for Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs Using Large Language Models
source_evidence.source_relative_path: Methods/181_KG-GPT A General Framework for Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs Using Large Language Models.pdf
source_evidence.text:
Abstract
While large language models (LLMs) have
made considerable advancements in under-
standing and generating unstructured text, their
application in structured data remains underex-
plored. Particularly, using LLMs for complex
reasoning tasks on knowledge graphs (KGs)
remains largely untouched. To address this,
we propose KG-GPT, a multi-purpose frame-
work leveraging LLMs for tasks employing
KGs. KG-GPT comprises three steps: Sentence
Segmentation, Graph Retrieval, and Inference,
each aimed at partitioning sentences, retriev-
ing relevant graph components, and deriving
logical conclusions, respectively. We evalu-
ate KG-GPT using KG-based fact verification
and KGQA benchmarks, with the model show-
ing competitive and robust performance, even
outperforming several fully-supervised models.
Our work, therefore, marks a significant step
in unifying structured and unstructured data
processing within the realm of LLMs.1
1

relation_review.evidence: 核对全部必要事实、引用与原文；没有来源时不得补造。
relation_review.semantics: 核对关系方向、实体角色、任务/实验条件和题干前提。
relation_review.uncertainty: 必要证据不足时明确说明缺口；反例允许纠正前提。

scoring_rules.primary: SupportRecall@5; within one fact unit supporting sources are OR, required fact units are AND.
scoring_rules.answer_review: Per-case atomic reference criteria, scored 0/1 each by a named reviewer; evidence support and citation location checked separately.
scoring_rules.graph_coverage: Source-backed expected subgraphs are a reference check, not measured retrieval success or answer correctness.
scoring_rules.denominator: 32 answerable questions; 24 cross-paper relation questions reported separately; 8 negative cases reported separately.
scoring_rules.interpretation: retrieval coverage, citation validity, graph-path coverage and semantic answer correctness are separate results; no assumption that graph wins.
scoring_rules.semantic_score: Number of supported satisfied atomic criteria / all criteria. This is not calculated by source ID recall.
scoring_rules.semantic_pass: All criteria satisfied with supporting citations; no critical unsupported claim. Negatives must correct/reject the premise within the evidence boundary.
critical_errors: 伪造继承/评测/全称优越性
混淆预算耗尽与正确答案
scoring_rules.reporting: Overview, per-category metrics, charts, latency, tokens and full paired details must coexist after real execution.

controls.generation_policy: All 40 questions require a full answer in a future comparison.
controls.graph_claim_source: Curated relations from frozen support excerpts, not model-generated claims.
controls.gold_input_policy: Only question text goes into retrieval/generation.
controls.runner_integration: pending: production Workflow still uses the old Neo4j graph
controls.fairness: Both arms use the same source corpus, models, reranker and declared budgets; only graph expansion differs.
controls.topology: Cross-paper cases compare source-backed subgraphs; no claim that all sources form one connected path.
